lessons.title: Shapes build a skyline
objectives: Name the shapes used in buildings
Draw a mosque skyline from circles, triangles, rectangles and arches
Colour it with a limited palette

keywords.def: a flat outline such as a circle or rectangle
a round roof shaped like half a ball
a tall tower beside a mosque
a curved opening at the top of a doorway or window

starter: What is a pattern? Give an example.

teach.heading: Shapes in buildings
bullets: Minarets are tall rectangles with a point
Arches are curved at the top
teach.note: Show a photo of a mosque or a house on screen. Ask children to name the shapes. Pupils need a pencil, a ruler if they have one, paper, crayons.

teach.heading: Building a skyline
bullets: Draw a flat line for the ground
Put a dome or triangle on top
teach.note: Model drawing step by step, slowly. Misconception: shapes must be perfect; stress that careful beats perfect.

teach.heading: Doors, windows and arches
bullets: Draw an arch with a curved top
Repeat shapes to make a pattern
teach.note: Link back to pattern. Ask: how many windows in your row? Encourage counting.

teach.heading: Choosing colours
teach.note: Limited palette teaches choice. Demonstrate colouring in one direction without gaps.

practice: Draw a circle, a triangle and a rectangle.
independent: Draw a skyline of five buildings using different shapes.
Add doors, windows and a pattern to each building.
exit: Name two shapes in your skyline.
lessons.homework: Draw a building you can see from your home using shapes.
lessons.send: SEND: provide shape outlines to trace; EAL: label shapes in English and home language; stretch: add a repeating pattern frieze along the roofline.

lessons.title: Light and dark: tone with a pencil
objectives: Press lightly and firmly to make light and dark
Make a tone strip from light to dark

keywords.def: how light or dark something is
to colour in with a pencil to make a dark area
pale, not much colour
deep, with lots of colour

starter: Draw a dome and a minaret.
Is a feather light or dark? Is night light or dark?

teach.heading: Light and dark
bullets: Tone means how light or dark
A pencil can make light or dark
Press softly for light, firmly for dark
teach.note: Pupils need a pencil and paper. Bismillah. Demonstrate pressing lightly and firmly on the camera.

teach.heading: A tone strip
teach.note: Model the strip. Misconception: the first box must be white and the last black; they just must change gradually.

teach.heading: Shading a leaf
bullets: Leave a light line down the middle
teach.note: A real leaf is helpful. Ask: where would the shadow be? Tone shows shape.

teach.heading: Look, compare, improve
bullets: Is it smooth from light to dark?
teach.note: Teach self-assessment: two stars and a wish with a partner or the teacher.

practice: Draw one light mark and one dark mark.
Which of these is darker: a pale grey or black?
independent: Shade a tone strip with five boxes from light to dark.
Draw a pear shape and use tone to make it look round.
exit: How do you make a dark mark with a pencil?
lessons.homework: Shade a tone strip with five boxes, then show a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: three boxes only; EAL: key words light, dark, press; stretch: shade a sphere with a shadow underneath.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Colour mixing, food landscapes and a fruit pot (Muck, Mess & Mixtures)
lessons.title: Mixing colours: primary to secondary
lessons.bigQuestion: How can three colours make every colour of the rainbow?
objectives: To understand how the three primary colours mix to make secondary colours
successCriteria: All: name the three primary colours
Most: mix two primaries to make a secondary colour
Some: place the colours in the right places on a colour wheel
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: noticing the colours in Allah's creation

keywords.def: red, yellow or blue: we cannot mix them from others
made by mixing two primaries
put together and stir
a circle that shows how colours go together

hook.text: If you could only have three paints, which would you choose and why?

islamicLink.text: Allah made the world full of colour. Allah says He sends rain and brings out fruits of different colours, and in the mountains are streaks of white and red of many shades (Fatir 35:27). When we mix colours, we notice the beauty Allah has put around us.

starter.q: Is paint a solid or a liquid?
What colour is a ripe banana?
Name a colour in the sky on a sunny day.

teach.heading: Primary colours
bullets: We cannot make them by mixing
teach.note: Show three blobs of paint. Ask: which colours do you see at home most?

teach.heading: Mix them
teach.note: Model on a plate: small amounts, stir with the brush, wash between colours.

teach.heading: The colour wheel
bullets: Primaries are opposite each other in a triangle
Orange sits between red and yellow
teach.note: Draw a circle split into six. Put red, yellow, blue in every other space. Ask: what goes between red and yellow?

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: Yellow and blue make green. Orange needs red; purple needs red and blue.

practice.q: Red and yellow make what colour?
practice.model:
Put a little red on the plate.
Add a little yellow.
Stir.
It turns orange.

practice.q: Which two primaries make purple?
Is green a primary or a secondary colour?

independent.q: Core: Paint a colour wheel: three primaries, then mix the three secondaries in the spaces between.
independent.a: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple in order round the circle
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: paint red, yellow and blue in every other space, then mix orange and paint it between red and yellow.

independent.q: Extend: Add more yellow to your green. What happens?
independent.a: It becomes a lighter, yellowy green

independent.q: Stretch: Mix all three primaries. What do you get?
independent.a: A muddy brown

exit.q: Which is a primary colour?
exit.a: Red

exit.q: Big question: how can three colours make every colour of the rainbow?
exit.a: By mixing two primaries we make secondaries, and mixing more makes other colours

lessons.homework: Mix food colouring in three cups of water with an adult and make orange, green and purple.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-filled paint pots and a printed wheel to colour. EAL: red, yellow, blue, mix with actions. Stretch: make two different greens and compare them.

Red, yellow and blue paint (or food colouring and water), a plate, a brush, a water pot, kitchen roll
An apron or old shirt; cover the table

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Colour mixing, food landscapes and a fruit pot (Muck, Mess & Mixtures)
lessons.title: Mixed media collage: a messy scene
lessons.bigQuestion: How can paper, fabric and paint work together in one picture?
objectives: To understand how to layer different materials to make a collage
successCriteria: All: cut or tear and stick materials to make a picture
Most: layer materials from the back to the front
Some: choose materials for their texture and colour

keywords.def: a picture made by sticking materials down
using more than one kind of material
one thing on top of another
how something feels or looks like it feels
the part at the back of a picture

hook.text: If you made a picture of a muddy puddle, what materials would you use?

teach.heading: What is a collage?
teach.note: Show a collage of a landscape (no people). Ask: what materials can you spot?

teach.heading: Layers
teach.note: Model tearing brown paper for mud and blue tissue for a puddle.

teach.heading: Texture
teach.note: Ask: which material would look like mud? Which like water?

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share results.

check.q: What do we stick down first?
check.why: Background first, then middle, then front details.

practice.q: Which material could show a shiny puddle?
practice.model:
A puddle is shiny and wet.
Foil is shiny.
So foil can show a puddle.

practice.q: What is the background of a muddy field picture?
Name a rough material.

independent.q: Core: Make a collage of a messy scene (a muddy garden or a rainy street). Background first, then middle, then details.
independent.a: A layered collage using at least three materials
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: tear blue paper for the sky, brown for mud, foil for a puddle, then leaves cut from green paper.

independent.q: Extend: Add one material for its texture.
independent.a: For example: crumpled tissue for mud

independent.q: Stretch: Tell the class why you chose one material.
independent.a: For example: I chose foil because puddles are shiny

exit.q: Collage means:
exit.a: A picture made by sticking materials down
options: A picture made by sticking materials down

exit.q: Big question: how can paper, fabric and paint work together in one picture?
exit.a: We layer them from back to front and choose them for their colour and texture

lessons.homework: Collect five scraps of different materials for your collage and finish it at home.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-cut shapes and a glue stick. EAL: tear, stick, layer with actions. Stretch: add a painted part to the collage (true mixed media).
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 2 curriculum map and long-term plans 2023-24; TGA Year 2 Curriculum Pack, Topic, Spring 1 Muck, Mess & Mixtures (Cornerstones Maestro: CHECK IN MAESTRO) (art and design strand)
Collage materials: coloured paper, tissue, foil, fabric scraps, card from packaging
Glue stick, child-safe scissors, a sheet of card as the base
Collage planning sheet (portal printable)

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Colour mixing, food landscapes and a fruit pot (Muck, Mess & Mixtures)
lessons.title: DT: design and make a fruit and yoghurt pot
lessons.bigQuestion: How do we make food that is safe, tasty and looks good?
objectives: To understand how to design, make and evaluate a simple food product hygienically
successCriteria: All: wash hands and make a fruit pot safely with an adult
Most: follow a design with layers
Some: evaluate the pot and say one change
lessons.smsc: Moral: hygiene and eating halal and good food

keywords.def: keeping clean to stop germs
a food we use in a recipe
one food on top of another
a plan of what we will make
say what went well and what to change

hook.text: Can a pot of fruit and yoghurt look like a muddy garden? What would you put on top?

islamicLink.text: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, taught that purity is half of faith (Sahih Muslim). Allah tells us to eat what is halal and good (al-Baqarah 2:168). So we wash our hands, check our food is halal and say Bismillah before we eat.

starter.q: What do we stick down first in a collage?
Is a banana natural or made by people?
Why do we wash our hands before eating?

teach.heading: Get ready
bullets: Tie back long hair, apron on
teach.note: Check that every ingredient is halal and that nobody has an allergy. Clean surfaces first.

teach.heading: Our design
teach.note: Draw the pot as layers and label them. Ask: why might we choose a see-through cup?

teach.heading: Make it safely
bullets: Use a table knife and a board
Cut soft fruit with an adult
teach.note: Model the bridge hold for cutting a banana: fingers away from the knife.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share results.

check.why: Hygiene first: wash hands before handling food.

practice.q: Put these in order: spoon in yoghurt, wash hands, add fruit.
practice.a: Wash hands, spoon in yoghurt, add fruit
practice.model:
Clean first: wash hands.
Then the bottom layer: yoghurt.
Then fruit on top.

practice.q: Why do we use a board when cutting?
practice.a: To keep the table clean and cut safely

practice.q: Name one ingredient in your design.

independent.q: Core: Make your fruit pot with an adult, following your layered design.
independent.a: A pot with three layers: yoghurt, fruit, crushed biscuit
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: two spoons of yoghurt, a layer of banana slices, then a sprinkle of crushed biscuit.

independent.q: Extend: Taste it and say one thing that went well.
independent.a: For example: the fruit made it sweet

independent.q: Stretch: Say one change you would make next time.
independent.a: For example: add more fruit or use a smaller cup

exit.q: Hygiene means:
exit.a: Keeping clean to stop germs

exit.q: Big question: how do we make food that is safe, tasty and looks good?
exit.a: Wash hands and keep things clean, follow the design in layers and evaluate the taste and look

lessons.homework: Make a fruit pot for someone in your family and ask them to give it a star rating out of three.
lessons.send: SEND: fruit pre-cut by an adult; pupil spoons the layers. EAL: wash, cut, spoon, layer with actions. Stretch: design a second pot with a new fruit.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 2 curriculum map and long-term plans 2023-24; TGA Year 2 Curriculum Pack, Topic, Spring 1 Muck, Mess & Mixtures (Cornerstones Maestro: CHECK IN MAESTRO) (DT strand)
Home practical guide and safety card: fruit and yoghurt pot (portal worksheet): halal and allergy check, adult supervises cutting
Fruit pot design and evaluation sheet (portal printable)
Yoghurt, a banana, soft berries, plain biscuits in a bag to crush, a clear cup
Table knife, chopping board, spoons, apron

pictures.alt: Yoghurt and berries in a glass
Washing hands with soap and water

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Still life and a paper bridge (Still Life and Can You Make a Paper Bridge?)
lessons.title: Still life drawing
lessons.bigQuestion: Can a bowl of fruit be a work of art?
objectives: To understand how artists observe and draw a still life arrangement
successCriteria: All: arrange and draw three objects
Most: draw the shapes in the right places
Some: add shading for light and dark
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: light makes shadows on the side away from it
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: noticing the beauty in everyday food Allah gives us

keywords.def: a picture of objects that do not move
look very carefully
put things in a place on purpose
a person who makes art
when one thing is in front of another

hook.text: Which three things from your kitchen would make the most interesting picture?

starter.q: A tall, narrow building is a:

teach.heading: What is a still life?
teach.note: The French artist Paul Cezanne painted many still lifes of apples.

teach.heading: Arrange
teach.note: Model arranging an apple, a cup and a lemon so they overlap.

teach.heading: Draw what you see
teach.note: Draw on camera.

model.problem: Draw an apple, a cup and a lemon
steps: Shade the side away from the light

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: Still life means objects that stay still, like fruit and cups.

practice.q: Draw a circle, then shade one side of it.
practice.a: A circle with shading on one side
practice.model:
I draw a circle lightly.
The light comes from the left.
I shade the right side.
Now it looks round like an apple.

independent.q: Core: Arrange three objects and draw them.
independent.a: A drawing of three objects in their places
independent.model: Teacher draws the apple first, then talks through where the cup goes.

independent.q: Extend: Make one object overlap another.
independent.a: One shape drawn partly behind another

independent.q: Stretch: Shade light and dark on every object.
independent.a: Shading on the side away from the light

exit.q: Observe means:
exit.a: Look very carefully

exit.q: Big question: can a bowl of fruit be a work of art?
exit.a: Yes: artists like Cezanne showed shape, colour and light in fruit

lessons.homework: Arrange three objects at home and draw them again from a different side.
lessons.send: SEND: draw two objects; thick pencil. EAL: arrange, draw, shade with actions. Stretch: draw the shadow on the table. No drawing of people or faces.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 2 curriculum map, art and design and DT long-term plans 2023-24; TGA Year 2 pack, Art and DT, Spring 2 Towers, Tunnels & Turrets (Still Life; Can You Make a Paper Bridge?) (CHECK IN MAESTRO)
Still life drawing frame (portal printable)
Fruit and household objects (an apple, a cup, a lemon)
Pencil and paper

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Still life and a paper bridge (Still Life and Can You Make a Paper Bridge?)
lessons.title: Can you make a paper bridge? (DT)
lessons.bigQuestion: How can one sheet of paper hold up coins?
objectives: To understand how folding paper makes a stronger bridge
successCriteria: All: make a flat and a folded paper bridge
Most: test each bridge with coins
Some: explain why the folded one is stronger
lessons.smsc: Social: being honest when we record results

keywords.def: something that crosses a gap
does not break or bend easily
bend paper over on itself
hold something up
try something to find out

hook.text: Will a flat sheet of paper hold one coin across a gap between two books?

teach.heading: Bridges
teach.note: Recap the Clifton Suspension Bridge.

teach.heading: Fold to make strong
teach.note: Show a flat sheet sagging, then a zigzag (concertina) fold.

teach.heading: Our fair test
bullets: Add coins one at a time
teach.note: Safety: wash hands after handling coins; keep coins away from mouths.

steps: Add one coin at a time

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.q: To make it a fair test we keep the same:
check.why: We keep the gap and paper size the same and change only the bridge shape.

practice.q: Predict: which will hold more coins, flat or zigzag?
practice.model:
Flat paper bends easily.
Zigzag folds stand up stiffly.
Stiff paper holds more.
I predict the zigzag holds more.

independent.q: Core: Test a flat and a zigzag bridge. Record the coins in the table.
independent.a: For example: flat 0 or 1 coin; zigzag several coins
independent.model: Teacher tests the flat bridge on camera and writes the number in the table.

independent.q: Extend: Try a rolled tube bridge.
independent.a: A result recorded for the tube

independent.q: Stretch: Say why the folds help.
independent.a: The folds make the paper stiff, so it does not bend under the coins

exit.q: Which bridge held more coins in most tests?
exit.a: Zigzag

exit.q: Big question: how can one sheet of paper hold up coins?
exit.a: Fold it into zigzags or tubes so it is stiff and strong

lessons.homework: Show your family the coin test and see if they can beat your best bridge.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-folded paper; count with an adult. EAL: fold, strong, test with actions. Stretch: try a wider gap and compare.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 2 curriculum map, art and design and DT long-term plans 2023-24; TGA Year 2 pack, Art and DT, Spring 2 Towers, Tunnels & Turrets (Still Life; Can You Make a Paper Bridge?) (CHECK IN MAESTRO)
Paper bridge test results table (portal printable; assessed)
A4 paper, two books of the same height, a ruler
Coins (1p or 2p) and a written safety guide: wash hands after, no coins near mouths

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Still life and a paper bridge (Still Life and Can You Make a Paper Bridge?)
lessons.title: Still life painting
lessons.bigQuestion: Can a painting of a vase of flowers be full of energy?
objectives: To understand how artists use colour and brush marks in a still life painting
successCriteria: All: paint a still life with three objects
Most: mix colours to match what you see
Some: use brush marks in the style of Van Gogh
lessons.smsc: Cultural: looking at work by famous artists

keywords.def: the way an artist usually makes their art
a mark made with a brush
put colours together to make a new one
the part behind the objects
how a surface looks or feels

hook.text: If you painted your still life with only three colours, which three would you choose?

teach.heading: Artists' styles
bullets: Van Gogh: thick, swirling brush marks
teach.note: Vincent van Gogh painted sunflowers in a vase. Look at objects and brush marks only.

teach.heading: Mixing colours
teach.note: Mix on a plate on camera.

teach.heading: Paint like Van Gogh
teach.note: Model painting a lemon.

steps: Mix yellow with a little white
Darker yellow on the shadow side
model.answer: A lemon with visible brush strokes

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: Blue and yellow are primary colours that mix to make green.

practice.q: Mix a green on your plate. Show me!
practice.a: A green mixed from blue and yellow
practice.model:
I put blue on the plate.
I add yellow.
I mix with the brush.
I see green.

independent.q: Core: Paint your still life from last time with three objects.
independent.a: A painting of three objects with mixed colours
independent.model: Teacher paints the lemon first using short strokes.

independent.q: Extend: Paint the background in one colour.
independent.a: A filled background

independent.q: Stretch: Use short Van Gogh strokes everywhere.
independent.a: Visible short strokes across the painting

exit.q: A brush stroke is:
exit.a: A mark made with a brush
options: A mark made with a brush

exit.q: Big question: can a still life be full of energy?
exit.a: Yes: bright colours and swirling strokes make it lively

lessons.homework: Paint one fruit at home using only short brush strokes.
lessons.send: SEND: chunky brush, two objects. EAL: mix, paint, stroke with actions. Stretch: try a Braque-style picture made of broken shapes. Objects only; no people.

Still life drawing from the previous art lesson
Paints (or felt tips), brush, a plate for mixing, water pot
Fruit and objects to paint

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Still life and a paper bridge (Still Life and Can You Make a Paper Bridge?)
lessons.title: Improve and test the paper bridge (DT)
lessons.bigQuestion: If we can only use paper and tape, how strong can our bridge be?
objectives: To understand how testing helps us improve a design
successCriteria: All: make an improved bridge
Most: test it fairly and record the result
Some: say what made it stronger
lessons.smsc: Moral: honest results and trying again

keywords.def: say what is good and what to improve
make better
plan what we will make
what happened in a test
does not break or bend easily

hook.text: What one change would make your zigzag bridge even stronger?

starter.q: A fair test keeps the same:
Who built the Clifton Suspension Bridge?

teach.heading: Our results
teach.note: Share last test's results.

teach.heading: Ideas to improve
teach.note: These are example results; we use our own.

teach.heading: Design, make, test
teach.note: Same gap and paper size as last time.

steps: Plan: add a flat deck on top
Tape the deck to the zigzag
Test: add coins one by one

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

options: To see if our change worked
check.why: Testing shows if our change made the bridge better.

practice.q: Draw your improved bridge plan and label one change.
practice.a: A plan with a labelled change
practice.model:
I draw the zigzag.
I add a flat deck on top.
I label it 'flat deck to spread the weight'.

independent.q: Core: Make and test your improved bridge. Record the coins.
independent.a: A result recorded and compared with the first test
independent.model: Teacher makes the deck version on camera and counts the coins aloud.

independent.q: Extend: Write: 'My bridge was better because ...'
independent.a: For example: the deck spread the weight

independent.q: Stretch: Suggest one more improvement.
independent.a: Any sensible change, for example smaller folds

exit.q: Evaluate means:
exit.a: Say what is good and what to improve
options: Say what is good and what to improve

exit.q: Big question: how strong can a paper bridge be?
exit.a: Our own result with a reason, for example the deck and folds held many coins

lessons.homework: Draw your best bridge for your family and explain why it was strong.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-cut deck; count with an adult. EAL: plan, make, test with pictures. Stretch: test with a wider gap. Wash hands after handling coins.

lessons.unit: Summer 1: Urban landscapes and a felt pouch (Street Detectives)
lessons.title: Urban landscape: the view from my window
lessons.bigQuestion: What shapes and colours make your street look like your street?
objectives: To understand how artists show an urban view using shapes, colour and near and far
successCriteria: All: paint or collage the shapes of buildings
Most: make near things big and far things small
Some: choose colours to match my view
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: features of our local area
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: noticing beauty in an ordinary view

keywords.def: to do with a town or city
a picture of a wide view
close to you; it looks bigger
a long way away; it looks smaller
a picture made by sticking on pieces

hook.text: Look out of your window. Which thing looks the biggest, and is it really the biggest?

starter.q: Name the artist we looked at in still life.

teach.heading: Urban landscapes
teach.note: Show a photo of a city skyline (buildings, no people).

teach.heading: Near and far
bullets: Far things go higher up the page
teach.note: Show a street photo: the near lamp post is taller than the far house.

teach.heading: Paint or collage
teach.note: Model a collage from magazine scraps: blue sky, grey roofs, a red door.

steps: Add near walls and doors big
model.answer: An urban landscape with near and far

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: Far things look smaller and higher up the picture.

practice.q: Show me a near shape and a far shape on your whiteboard.
practice.a: A big shape low down and a small shape higher up
practice.model:
Near: I draw a big square low down.
Far: I draw a small square higher up.

practice.q: Is a city urban or not urban?

independent.q: Core: Paint or collage the view from your window, with near things big and far things small.
independent.a: An urban landscape with sky, buildings and near and far shown
independent.model: Teacher shows the model collage step by step.

independent.q: Extend: Add three details, such as windows, a lamp post or a tree.
independent.a: Three details added

independent.q: Stretch: Say which colours you mixed and why.
independent.a: For example: grey from black and white for the roofs

exit.q: Urban means to do with a:

exit.q: Big question: what makes your street look like your street?
exit.a: Its own shapes and colours: roofs, doors, trees and sky

lessons.homework: Photograph your finished landscape and show it to your family; say which part is near and which is far.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-cut shapes for collage. EAL: near, far, big, small with gestures. Stretch: add a shadow on one side of each building.

Most: sew a running stitch

keywords.def: cloth, like felt or cotton
one loop of thread through fabric
in and out in a straight line
fix two things together
thin string used for sewing

hook.text: What could you keep in a small pouch that you made yourself?

teach.heading: Safe sewing
bullets: Needle back in its pot after use
teach.note: Plastic or large-eye blunt needles only. Adult supervision throughout.

teach.heading: Running stitch
teach.note: Spoken rhythm (no song): up, down, up, down.

teach.heading: Make the pouch
bullets: Two felt rectangles, one on top
teach.note: Model the pouch live on camera.

steps: Thread the needle and knot the end
Stitch the bottom and other side
model.answer: A pouch open at the top

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.q: Which side do we leave open?
check.why: The open top lets us put things in; the other three sides are stitched.

practice.q: Show me: point to where the next stitch goes.
practice.a: A spot a little further along the line
practice.model:
My last stitch ended here.
I leave a small gap.
The next stitch goes in after the gap.

practice.q: Why do we tie a knot?
practice.a: So the thread does not pull out

independent.q: Core: Sew two felt rectangles together on three sides with running stitch, with an adult helping.
independent.a: A pouch with stitches along three sides and the top open
independent.model: Teacher shows the model pouch and the first three stitches.

independent.q: Extend: Decorate the front with a felt shape or button (adult helps).
independent.a: A decoration added

independent.q: Stretch: Say one thing that went well and one thing to improve.
independent.a: For example: even stitches; the knot came undone

exit.q: Running stitch goes:
exit.a: In and out

exit.q: Big question: how do two flat pieces become a pouch?
exit.a: We join three sides with stitches and leave the top open

lessons.homework: Finish your pouch at home with an adult and keep something special in it, such as your miswak or prayer beads.
lessons.send: SEND: holes pre-punched in the felt; adult threads the needle. EAL: needle, thread, stitch shown on camera. Stretch: try a whip stitch on the edge.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 2 curriculum map, art and design long-term plan and DT long-term plan 2023-24; TGA Year 2 pack, Art and DT, Summer 1 Street Detectives (CHECK IN MAESTRO)
Felt (two rectangles about 10 cm by 12 cm), thick thread or wool, large blunt needle, scissors (adult supervision)
Pouch steps sheet (portal printable)

lessons.unit: Summer 2: Observational drawing, pressed flowers and a scented sachet (The Scented Garden)
lessons.title: DT: design and make a fragrant sachet
lessons.bigQuestion: Which smells make you feel calm and happy?
objectives: To understand how to design, make and evaluate a fragrant sachet for a purpose
successCriteria: All: choose dried herbs or petals for a scent
Most: make a sachet that holds its filling
Some: evaluate the sachet against my design
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: the parts of plants we dry and use
lessons.smsc: Social: making a gift to show care for someone

keywords.def: having a nice smell
a small cloth bag with something inside
plan what you will make
with the water taken out
say what went well and what to change

hook.text: If you made a small bag of nice smells for someone you love, what would you put in it?

starter.q: Name a plant with a nice smell.

teach.heading: What is it for?
bullets: A sachet for a drawer or wardrobe
teach.note: Design starts with who it is for and what it must do.

teach.heading: Choose a scent
bullets: Whole cloves or a cinnamon stick
teach.note: Only dry plants and spices; no perfume or anything with alcohol. Check for allergies.

teach.heading: Make it
bullets: Cut a cloth circle or square
Put two spoonfuls in the middle
Gather up and tie tightly, or sew
teach.note: Model the tie method. Pupils who can sew may use running stitch from the felt pouch.

steps: Cut a 20 cm square of cloth
Tie tightly with ribbon or wool
model.answer: A sachet that does not leak

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

options: Hold its filling and smell nice
check.why: Its job is to hold the dried filling and give off a nice smell.

practice.q: Who is your sachet for, and where will it go?
practice.a: For example: for my mother's drawer
practice.model:
I think of someone I want to give it to.
I think where they keep clothes.
My sachet is for my sister's wardrobe.

practice.q: Why must the filling be dried?
How will you close your sachet?
practice.a: Tie with ribbon or sew with running stitch

independent.q: Core: Draw and label your design (cloth, filling, how it closes), then make the sachet with an adult.
independent.a: A labelled design and a finished sachet that does not leak
independent.model: Teacher shows a labelled design: 'blue cloth, lavender, tied with ribbon'.

independent.q: Extend: Shake your sachet gently: does it leak? Fix it if it does.
independent.a: No leaks, or retied tighter

independent.q: Stretch: Evaluate: what would you change next time?
independent.a: For example: use thicker cloth so the petals do not poke out

exit.q: Fragrant means:
exit.a: Having a nice smell

exit.q: Big question: which smell did you choose, and why?
exit.a: For example: lavender because it smells calm

lessons.homework: Give your sachet to the person you made it for and ask what they think of the smell.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-cut cloth and a spoon; adult ties the knot with the pupil. EAL: design words with pictures. Stretch: sew the sachet closed with running stitch.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 2 curriculum map, art and design long-term plan and DT long-term plan 2023-24; TGA Year 2 pack, Art and DT, Summer 2 The Scented Garden (CHECK IN MAESTRO)
Design and evaluate sheet (portal printable)
Household items: an old clean cloth or handkerchief, scissors (with an adult), ribbon or wool, dried lavender, rose petals, mint, rosemary or whole cloves (alcohol-free; check allergies)

pictures.alt: A small cloth bag of lavender

lessons.unit: Summer 2: Observational drawing, pressed flowers and a scented sachet (The Scented Garden)
lessons.title: Look closely: drawing and pressing a flower; end-of-year quiz
lessons.bigQuestion: How many details can you spot in one flower if you look for a whole minute?
objectives: To understand how to observe closely and record a flower in a careful drawing
successCriteria: All: draw the shape of the petals and leaves I can see
Most: label the parts of the flower in my drawing
Some: press a flower safely to keep it
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: wonder at the detail in a single flower

keywords.def: look very closely
a small part you notice when you look closely
flatten something to keep it
write the name of a part
a coloured part of a flower

hook.text: Choose one flower or leaf near you. What can you see when you look really closely?

islamicLink.text: Allah tells us that the many colours of the things He has spread on the earth are a sign for people who remember (An-Nahl 16:13). When we look closely at a flower, we notice Allah's work.

teach.heading: Look for one minute
bullets: Notice the shape of each leaf
teach.note: Time one minute of silent looking. Pupils share one detail in the chat.

teach.heading: Draw what you see
bullets: Draw the shape, then the details
teach.note: Model a daisy: centre circle, then petals one by one.

steps: Add petals one at a time
Draw the stem and a leaf

teach.heading: Press a flower
bullets: Place it inside folded kitchen paper
Put it in a heavy book
teach.note: Ask an adult before picking; choose a small flat flower from your own garden or a shop bunch.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: Observing means looking carefully to notice details.

practice.q: Quiz 1: Which part of a plant takes in water? A) root B) petal C) flower
practice.model:
I think back to our plant parts lesson.
Roots are under the soil.
They take in water, so the answer is root.

practice.q: Quiz 2: Which continent is the UK in?
Quiz 3: Name the ocean round Antarctica.

independent.q: Core: Draw your flower carefully and label petal, stem, leaf (and root if you can see it).
independent.a: A careful observational drawing with correct labels
independent.model: Teacher starts the daisy drawing from the model slide.

independent.q: Extend: Press your flower in a heavy book with an adult.
independent.a: A flower placed in kitchen paper in a heavy book

independent.q: Stretch: Add three tiny details you noticed.
independent.a: For example: lines on the petals, a hairy stem, a jagged leaf edge

exit.q: Quiz 4: How many oceans are there?
exit.a: Five

exit.q: Big question: how many details did you spot in one flower?
exit.a: Any number with examples, for example: lines on petals and a hairy stem

lessons.homework: In two weeks, take your pressed flower out and stick it onto card to make a picture.
lessons.send: SEND: a large flower photo to draw from and labels to stick on. EAL: part names with pictures. Stretch: shade the petals to show light and dark.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 2 curriculum map, art and design long-term plan and DT long-term plan 2023-24; TGA Year 2 pack, Art and DT, Summer 2 The Scented Garden (CHECK IN MAESTRO)
Year 2 end-of-year quiz: plant labels and continents and oceans (portal Forms quiz)
Labelled drawing sheet (portal printable)
A flower or leaf from home, kitchen paper, a heavy book, pencil and coloured pencils
